section_summary.extract_value: This Introduction reviews theories and empirical evidence that exposure to natural environments and connectedness to nature promote psychological well-being and may influence body image. It cites prior qualitative, experimental, and survey studies (including Swami et al., 2016) and notes measures such as the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its revision BAS-2; no specific studies or sample-level details (e.g., N, country, age, BMI) for 'Study 1' or similar are reported in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Representative sentences: 'There is now ample and credible evidence demonstrating that exposure to natural environments ... has health-promoting qualities.'; 'connectedness to nature was directly associated with body appreciation–operationalised using the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS; Avalos, Tylka, & Wood-Barcalow, 2005) ... in women (r = .32) but not in men (r = .10; Swami, von Nordheim, et al., 2016).'; 'the BAS has recently been revised ... (BAS-2; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015a, 2015b).'
